project: defender — an LLM SOC-analyst agent (python, pytest, uv)

gate.test: cd defender && uv run pytest tests/ -m "not llm and not live"
checks: the baseline-ratcheted custom lints under scripts/lint/lint_*.py (monkeypatch, unsafe-jsonl-io, raw-git-subprocess, unanchored-default, vulture, duplicate-helpers, …) — each blocks only on a NEW finding, and each documents an inline-suppression escape hatch in its own module
gate.notes: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is the source of truth — run what it runs; don't trust this list to stay current. Running in a git worktree? The shared `.venv` editable install points at the main checkout — prepend `PYTHONPATH=<worktree-root>` to the pytest call or you test the wrong tree.

tests.harness: defender/tests/e2e/_replay_harness.py — a new scenario is a few lines of `Turn(...)`, not fresh plumbing. Build on it rather than inventing parallel machinery.
tests.idioms: Fakes enter through the entry point's injection seams (a `deps` parameter, a constructor argument), never `monkeypatch.setattr` — CI ratchets new setattr sites (`scripts/lint/lint_monkeypatch.py`).

run_dir.note: Four writers were added after #771's phase-F reconciliation found the same hole in three instruments at once. The driver's fault-exit trace write (`write_text("")` onto the fixed tool_trace.jsonl name observe.write_trace also owns) is one of the two sites that issue reported and was missing from the test census, the write lint's gate list AND this list. The queries-table append is the query tool's SECOND artifact — the payload write was censused, the table was not. The lead-claim hook and the atomic helper are the two the original grep could not see. EVERY ENTRY MUST NAME A SYMBOL THAT RESOLVES: three of the four added here did not (a leading underscore the driver's entry point does not have, an actor id where the code symbol was `_revert_strays`, and a render-lane function renamed at some point), and a resolver following a name that resolves to nothing gets the same answer as one following a row that was never written. This list seeds the next run's census, so a gap here becomes a gap in every downstream instrument. `scrub` stays under readers deliberately: #771's scan verdict is written OUTSIDE the tree it judges (§7 D8), so the walk remains a pure reader of the run dir and the marker belongs to no run-dir writer census.

investigation_md.note: Declared by #996's grounding, because the clerk port moves WHO writes this file and the design's own census said the runtime writers were the two document tools. THEY ARE SIX, and the four extra are the ones a `_tool_append_block` reference walk cannot see: `_tool_write_file`/`_tool_edit_file` reach it whenever the operand resolves to `<run_dir>/investigation.md` (screened by `permission.decide_write`'s invlang schema plus `_files._closed_for_investigation_write`, NOT by the append lane), `lead_zero._declare_l_finding` seeds lead-0's `:L findings` row through `write_guarded` before MAIN's first turn, and `branch/_seed.seed_investigation` writes a sibling run's whole document from the source's prefix. The last two are host frames with no `decide_write` in front of them; both call `validate_artifact` themselves and say so in their own docstrings (#961/#964's class, sites two and three). THE VERB NAME IS PART OF THIS ROOT'S CONTRACT, which is the trap #996 walks into: four production readers key on the STRING "append_block" rather than on any symbol — `compaction.apply_writes` (replays the write from the transcript), `branch/_frontier.fence_count_at` (counts landed fences for a branch point, and `seed_investigation` above depends on its answer), `hooks/budget_enforcer._MAIN_TAIL_TOOLS` (the tier that keeps MAIN's only writer un-refusable at the cap) and `scripts/visualize/visualize_data` (the write lane's pathless-verb list). None is a call edge, so no resolver reaches them; a change that renames MAIN's writer must move all four in the same commit. Readers listed are the ones that ask this document a QUESTION the port changes the answer to; the learning-side archive/persist copies are omitted deliberately — they move bytes without reading them.

drain_worktree.note: #869's grounding added the two writers the SPAWNED-AGENT-ONLY reading of this root missed. `synthesize_drafts` is a HOST-side writer into the worktree's catalog — it mkdir+writes `<catalog>/{system}/_draft/{suffix}.md` from a model-supplied `query_id` BEFORE the agent is spawned, which is the whole of #869's C12 reachability finding and was invisible to a census that only listed the agent's file tools. `commit_corpus` is the sink's actual commit (git add over the `defender/skills` pathspec) and the last gate any path rule sits in front of. The readers added are the ones that ask the tree a MEMBERSHIP question: the git-status scope walk that applies the per-actor path rule, the `_draft/` discovery that turns a directory name into a handoff `system`, and the two per-actor path rules themselves. THE THIRD READER THIS ORIGINALLY LISTED WAS `pitfalls_curator.py::_is_real_system`, THE `SKILL.md` PROBE — and #869 DELETES that symbol, so the entry that seeds the next run's census would have named a symbol resolving to nothing, which this block's own rule forbids and which a resolver cannot distinguish from a row nobody wrote. Replaced with the threaded membership readers that survive the change (`_pitfalls_path_rule`, `_skills_path_rule`); the resolver they are threaded from, `learning/leads/declared_systems.py::declared_systems`, is deliberately NOT listed yet because it does not exist until write-code-from-spec builds it — add it in the same commit that does, or this list under-counts the membership readers by one.

episode_dir.note: Declared by #947's grounding. AT b8a63e66 `capture.py:130-136` composes it as `resolve_runs_base()/'episodes'/<id>/` — a sibling of the run dirs, inside the runs base. #947 MOVES BOTH ENDS OF THAT, and this note is written against the design, not the base: (1) the episodes root becomes a CONFIGURED location (`DEFENDER_EPISODES_BASE`), outside both the runs base and the checkout, with NO default derivation — a reader that re-derives it from the runs base silently restores the containment hole the relocation closed (#947 §7 round 2, F5-EPISODE-ROOT); and (2) the three sibling run dirs move UNDER it, at `{episode_dir}/runs/`, so the episode dir is a PARENT of run dirs rather than their sibling. `cli.py::episode_dir_for` is the symbol whose semantics change: it is the production resolver every reader of an episode must go through once the root is configured, and the one to follow instead of re-composing a path. The old safety clause here read 'a SIBLING of the run dirs, never inside one, so it is not bound into any box' — that is verbatim the reason `capture.py:134`'s waiver states, and #947 REFUTES it on that reason (claim C26): the episode dir now contains three rw box binds. The conclusion survives on a different ground, recorded as an examined no: the bind is the run dir alone, `served/` and `worlds/` stay unreachable from inside a box, and every archive read goes through the `_run_paths.artifact_file` / `stage_tables` screens. Rewrite `capture.py:134`'s waiver text in the same commit that moves the root. Today it holds only `served/`: `prime_base` writes `served/base.jsonl` once and `Ledger.record` appends `served/<world_id>.jsonl`, one writer per file — which is the whole of the launcher's parallel-safety premise. The directory is created as a side effect of `_io.append_jsonl`'s parent mkdir, NOT through `guarded_mkdir`, and NOTHING anywhere removes an episode dir: both `prepare_episode` and `prime_base` treat an existing one as a permanent refusal. #947 adds family.yaml, staged.yaml, review.yaml, provenance.json, worlds/<X>/ AND runs/<sibling>/ here — add those writers (staging.py, review.py, archive.py, _family.py) IN THE COMMIT THAT CREATES THEM, not before: a row naming a symbol that resolves to nothing is indistinguishable to a resolver from a row nobody wrote. ADDED IN THE COMMIT THAT CREATED THEM, as the sentence above requires: `write_family` (family.yaml), `record_staged` and `_record_teardown_failure` (staged.yaml and the teardown block of review.yaml), `review` (review.yaml), `archive_episode` (worlds/<X>/), and `cli._record_episode_outcome` / `_write_family_stamp` (the episode's own outcome and its provenance.json). The readers gain the two derived readers, the staging record's own reader and the manifest loader.

elastic_corpus.note: Declared by #947's grounding as an EMPTY-WRITER root, which is the fact worth recording: at b8a63e66 nothing in defender/ creates an Elasticsearch index or alias (re-verified: the only `_aliases`/`put_alias` hits are a yaml dumper flag and the model-provider alias table). Every listed reader reaches the cluster through the one read-confined door, `elastic_adapter._http_json` -> `confinement.guard_outbound` -> `confine_read_endpoint(verb_class='r')`, whose elastic allowlist is exactly `/*/_search POST`, `/_query POST`, `/_cluster/health GET`, `/api/status GET`. #947's corpus staging is the FIRST writer; it must call `transport.docker_exec_curl` directly, and note that `guard_outbound` is also the capture recorder, so a write door that skips it records nothing anywhere but `staged.yaml`. #947 LANDS THAT FIRST WRITER and this row now names it: `staging._Door` reaches `docker_exec_curl` directly with PUT/POST/DELETE, outside `guard_outbound`, so `staged.yaml` is the only record any of these writes happened. The host-side reads are listed beside them because `_count` and `_resolve/index` are deliberately absent from the adapter's read allowlist — they exist only on this door.

conventions.dangerLens: adversarial input — alert data is attacker-influenced by definition, and malicious input is well-formed on purpose. Use this as write-tests' fourth enumeration lens unless the change's danger zone is clearly elsewhere (environment/resource, or concurrency when the design admits parallel invocation).

codeGraph.notes: defender is a namespace package (no defender/__init__.py; pyproject at defender/, not the repo root), so pyrefly's import root defaults to defender/ and `defender.x` imports silently resolve to Unknown. searchPath is relative to configDir: `..` = repo root (makes `defender` a top-level package, mirroring pytest's pythonpath=['..']), `.` = defender/. The pyrefly-refs helper writes a temp configDir/pyrefly.toml from these and removes it per run.
